status: DRAFT: written from general chest radiograph criteria, needs radiologist review
state_after_gate: An image is attached. It is a frontal chest X-ray.

gate.q: Is the image taken from the front?
Are both lungs fully visible in the image?
Is the image sharp and well exposed?
Is the chest rotated or tilted by more than 20 degrees?
Is the whole rib cage visible from the collar bones down to below the diaphragm?
Is the image a radiograph rather than a photograph, drawing or screenshot?
Is the image free of large text or markers covering the lungs?
Is the contrast good enough to see the ribs through the lungs?
Is the patient positioned straight, with the collar bones level?

features.q: Is there a patchy or solid white area in either lung?
Is the white area limited to one part of one lung?
Are both lung fields equally dark with no white patches?
Is the outline of the heart sharp on both sides?
Is the edge of each diaphragm sharp and clearly visible?
Are the angles between the diaphragm and the chest wall sharp on both sides?
Are there thickened lines radiating from the centre of the lungs?
Is there a fluffy or hazy whiteness spread over a large part of a lung?
Are the lungs overinflated, with flattened diaphragms?
Is there a dark branching air line inside a white area?
Are tubes, wires or other devices visible on the chest?
Is the heart enlarged compared with the width of the chest?
Are the fine lines of the lung pattern evenly spread across both lungs?
Is one lung visibly whiter than the other?
Are the lung fields transparent enough to see the ribs through them in both lungs?
Is the trachea in the midline?
Is there air or fluid at the edge of either lung, between the lung and the ribs?
Is the right half of the diaphragm higher than the left half or the other way round by more than a rib?
Is there any cloudy area that blends into the heart shadow?
Does either lung look smaller than the other?

discriminators.q: Is the white area in the lower part of a lung?
Is the white area wedge shaped and touching the chest wall?
Does a white area hide the edge of the heart or of a diaphragm?
Is a white area present in both lungs?
Is there a thin line of fluid along the side of a lung?
Are there small scattered white spots like nodules?
Is the white area made of many small patches joined together?
Is a white area visible behind the heart?
Is there a visible border of a lobe, like a straight line between white and dark lung?
Are the white areas symmetric left and right, like an even haze?
Is the rib pattern clearly visible through every part of both lungs?
Is the heart shadow clearly separated from the lung on both sides?

deep.q: Does the white area have air-filled dark tubes running through it?
Does the white area end sharply at a straight line?
Is the white area denser than the soft tissue of the heart?
Is the white area in the middle part of the lung and not the top?
Do the vessels at the base of the lungs look sharp?
Are both sides of the diaphragm clearly curved and dome shaped?
Are the airways next to the heart clearly visible?
Is there a bright spot in the lung that could be a nodule or a button?
